questions.stem:
Articles made on a lathe are subject to three kinds of defect, $A$, $B$ or $C$. A sample of 1000 articles was inspected and the following results were obtained.
31 had a type $A$ defect
37 had a type $B$ defect
42 had a type $C$ defect
11 had both type $A$ and type $B$ defects
13 had both type $B$ and type $C$ defects
10 had both type $A$ and type $C$ defects
6 had all three types of defect.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Draw a Venn diagram to represent these data.
(6)
parts.mark_scheme: (a) 6: B1. Subtract: M1. 4, 5, 7: A1. Subtract: M1. 16, 19, 25: A1. Box & 918: B1

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Find the probability that a randomly selected article from this sample had
(b) no defects,
(1)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) no more than one of these defects.
(2)

parts.label: d
parts.text:
An article selected at random from this sample had only one defect.
(d) Find the probability that it was a type $B$ defect.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme: (d) P($B$|Only 1 defect) = P($B$ and 1 defect)/P(1 defect) = $\frac{19/1000}{(16+19+25)/1000}$: M1: conditional prob. = 19/60: A1(ft): or 0.316 or 0.317

parts.label: e
parts.text:
Two different articles were selected at random from this sample.
(e) Find the probability that both had type $B$ defects.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme: (e) P(Both had type $B$) = $\frac{37}{1000} \times \frac{36}{999}$: M1: theirs from $B$ $\times$ ... = 37/27750 or 0.00133 or equivalent: A1: cao

questions.question_text:
Articles made on a lathe are subject to three kinds of defect, $A$, $B$ or $C$. A sample of 1000 articles was inspected and the following results were obtained.
31 had a type $A$ defect
37 had a type $B$ defect
42 had a type $C$ defect
11 had both type $A$ and type $B$ defects
13 had both type $B$ and type $C$ defects
10 had both type $A$ and type $C$ defects
6 had all three types of defect.
(a) Draw a Venn diagram to represent these data.
(6)
Find the probability that a randomly selected article from this sample had
(b) no defects,
(1)
(c) no more than one of these defects.
(2)
An article selected at random from this sample had only one defect.
(d) Find the probability that it was a type $B$ defect.
(2)
Two different articles were selected at random from this sample.
(e) Find the probability that both had type $B$ defects.
(2)
questions.mark_scheme_text:
(a) 6: B1. Subtract: M1. 4, 5, 7: A1. Subtract: M1. 16, 19, 25: A1. Box & 918: B1
(b) P(No defects) = 918/1000 = 0.918: B1(ft)
(c) P(No more than 1) = (918+16+19+25)/1000 OR $1 - (5+6+4+7)/1000$: M1. = 0.978: A1(ft)
(d) P($B$|Only 1 defect) = P($B$ and 1 defect)/P(1 defect) = $\frac{19/1000}{(16+19+25)/1000}$: M1: conditional prob. = 19/60: A1(ft): or 0.316 or 0.317
(e) P(Both had type $B$) = $\frac{37}{1000} \times \frac{36}{999}$: M1: theirs from $B$ $\times$ ... = 37/27750 or 0.00133 or equivalent: A1: cao

questions.question_text:
A discrete random variable is such that each of its values is assumed to be equally likely.
(a) Write down the name of the distribution that could be used to model this random variable.
(1)
(b) Give an example of such a distribution.
(1)
(c) Comment on the assumption that each value is equally likely.
(2)
(d) Suggest how you might refine the model in part (a).
(2)
questions.mark_scheme_text:
(a) (Discrete) Uniform: B1
(b) e.g. Tossing a fair dice / coin: B1g
(c) Useful in theory - allows problems to be modelled: B1g. Not necessarily true in practice: B1h
(d) Carry out an experiment: B1g. to establish probabilities: B1h

questions.stem:
The random variable $X$ is normally distributed with mean 79 and variance 144.
Find

parts.label: c
parts.text:
It is known that $\mathrm{P}(79-a \leqslant X \leqslant 79+b) = 0.6463$. This information is shown in the figure below.
Given that $\mathrm{P}(X \geqslant 79+b) = 2\mathrm{P}(X \leqslant 79-a)$,
(c) show that the area of the shaded region is 0.1179.
(3)

parts.label: d
parts.mark_scheme: (d) $\mathrm{P}(X \leqslant 79+b) = 0.7642$: B1: implied. $\Rightarrow \frac{b}{12} = 0.72$: M1A1: standardise LHS = z-value, all correct. $b = 8.64$: A1: 3sf

questions.question_text:
The random variable $X$ is normally distributed with mean 79 and variance 144.
Find
(a) $\mathrm{P}(X<70)$,
(3)
(b) $\mathrm{P}(64<X<96)$.
(3)
It is known that $\mathrm{P}(79-a \leqslant X \leqslant 79+b) = 0.6463$. This information is shown in the figure below.
Given that $\mathrm{P}(X \geqslant 79+b) = 2\mathrm{P}(X \leqslant 79-a)$,
(c) show that the area of the shaded region is 0.1179.
(3)
(d) Find the value of $b$.
(4)
questions.mark_scheme_text:
(a) $\mathrm{P}(X<70) = \mathrm{P}(Z<\frac{70-79}{12})$: M1: standardise 79, 12 or 79, 144. $= \mathrm{P}(Z<-0.75) = 0.2266$: A1A1: + or -0.75, 0.2266
(b) $\mathrm{P}(64<X<96) = \mathrm{P}(\frac{64-79}{12}<Z<\frac{96-79}{12})$: M1: standardise both, 79 & 12 only. + or -1.25 & 1.42, 0.8166: A1,A1: Accept 0.8160-0.8170
(c) Shaded area $= \frac{1}{3}(1-0.6463)$: M1A1. $= 0.1179$: A1: cso
(d) $\mathrm{P}(X \leqslant 79+b) = 0.7642$: B1: implied. $\Rightarrow \frac{b}{12} = 0.72$: M1A1: standardise LHS = z-value, all correct. $b = 8.64$: A1: 3sf
